chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala', who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who prays two rak'ahs of the obligatory prayer and does not sit until he bows for the third, so he said: 'He completes his prayer, then gives the salutation, and prostrates the two prostrations of forgetfulness while sitting, before he speaks.'
ai.seo_question: What should one do if they stand up for the third rak'ah without sitting in an obligatory prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from Sahih al-Tusi clarifies the procedural remedy for a specific structural error in prayer, emphasizing that the validity of the prayer remains intact despite the omission of the intermediate sitting. It highlights the Shia jurisprudential preference for performing sujadat al-sahw after the final salutation (tashahhud and salam) in cases of minor omissions, ensuring the worshipper rectifies the mistake without invalidating the prayer's core components.
